## 3. Transition tables

Eventual shares (published table) are the published table and tail from month 0 (`eventualProbabilities`; possibly θ-scaled or laddered), project-weighted. The two raw columns are the Aalen–Johansen incidence at the end of observation of the pathway’s own spells in the pooled window (preApplication: all pathways), with no tail: unweighted (each spell counts once) and unit-weighted (each spell weighted by its net units). Comparing the raw pair shows the effect of weighting; comparing the published table with the unweighted column shows the effect of the table construction and tail.

## 4. Construction duration: TCO versus completed_date

Over 4 completed histories with a construction start and permit rows with a `complete_day`: median construction duration to the history's completion (first TCO/CFC, else permit `completed_date`) = 882.5 days (28.9944 months); to the earliest permit `complete_day` = 882.5 days (28.9944 months); difference 0 days. The medians hide the cases where the two dates differ: 0 of them have a completion day different from the earliest permit `complete_day`; paired median of (history completion − earliest permit `complete_day`) over them = none days. TCO data start in 2018, so earlier completions are dated later.

### Choice model

A multinomial logit over 0, 1, 2 and 3+ cars per household (0 the base), in the structure of MTC Travel Model Two and ActivitySim's auto_ownership, refitted to SF data (provenance tier 1: fitted: ACS PUMS household terms, ACS B25044 block-group location terms and constants).
Stage 1, household terms: 160 PUMS households (weights WGTP) with the PUMA's mean density and access; log-likelihood -4364, 7 Newton iterations.
Stage 2, location terms: household terms fixed, the start households of 3 block groups; log-likelihood -76.9, 7 iterations.
Standard errors are stated at the PUMS sample size (160 records); stage 2's are indicative only (its shares are B25044 block-group estimates). A dropped term is one the data cannot identify (no variation, or fewer than 3 PUMAs or peopled block groups): its coefficient is 0.
Density is start households per hectare of land (TIGER ALAND); access is the transit grid's value, homes-weighted over each block group's lots.

TM2 nests car counts (nesting coefficients 0.3 and 0.668), so its values are not MNL-comparable in scale.

### Transit access measure

The grid measure raises stage 2's log-likelihood by 0.1629 over density alone (-77.07 without access). No jobs-reachable measure can be built from the lock (it has no jobs-by-location source), so the comparison the spec allows was not made and the grid stays.

### Fit by block group

Before the zone constants (the across-zone terms alone), over 3 block groups with B25044 households: zero-car share error median 2.16 points, 90th percentile 7.39 points, mean 3.73 points; largest error at any level median 8.01 points, 90th percentile 24.82 points.
Shrinkage: each block group's B25044 shares are pulled toward the model's (empirical Bayes, share* = (n obs + n0 pred) / (n + n0)) with n0 = 39.87, by the method of moments on the dispersion of observed against predicted shares beyond sampling variance. An observed zero level keeps a nonzero share.
n is each block group's effective sample size from its B25044 margins of error (n_eff = sum p(1-p) / sum SE(p)^2 over the four levels, SE = MOE / 1.645; a level's MOE is the Census rule for a sum: every nonzero cell's MOE in quadrature plus only the largest MOE among its zero-estimate cells, per the Census Bureau's "Understanding and Using American Community Survey Data" (2020), ch. 8): median 70.52 against a median 480 estimated households; 0 block groups had no margins and take their estimated households.
Constants: 3 block groups fitted to the shrunk shares (largest difference 4.7e-11), range -0.655 to 0.2345; fitted to the raw B25044 shares instead (an observed zero held at 1e-9) they would range -1.377 to 0.3316. 0 block groups have no B25044 households (constants 0), 0 no start household (the citywide type mix stands in); 0 observed-zero shares.
After the constants, against the raw B25044 shares: zero-car share error median 1.15 points, 90th percentile 4.11 points, mean 1.93 points; largest error at any level median 2.47 points, 90th percentile 11.51 points.

Largest zero-car errors after the constants (3):

| Block group | Start households | B25044 households | B25044 no car | Before | After |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 060759901002 | 14 | 380 | 23.7% | 16.3% | 19.6% |
| 060759901003 | 41 | 650 | 26.2% | 24.0% | 25.0% |
| 060759901001 | 14 | 480 | 27.1% | 28.7% | 27.6% |

Start population: each block group's households are raked to share* as the vehicle margin (B25009 tenure by size and B19001 income as before), so at month 0 they hold the model's shares up to rounding: zero-car gap median 1.86 points, 90th percentile 6.70 points, households-weighted mean 4.55 points; the largest gap at any level, 18.66 points, is in a block group of 14 households (one household moves a share by 1/n).

Households: 69 start households (assessor homes times the occupied share) against 1510 in B25044; shares are compared, not totals. The start households hold the model's shares (first two columns, up to rounding). The model columns are the same model and constants: they differ only in where the assessor homes (times the occupied share) sit against where ACS counts households. The last two differ by the shrinkage.

### Cross-checks

Cars: the model gives 97 household cars (3+ households at 3.628, the PUMS mean), 1.401 per household.
DMV: no registrations in the lock; no cross-check.

### Moves

Move rates from PUMS 2020-2024 households by when they moved in (MV 1, within 12 months), 160 records: owners 5.2% a year (0.446% a month, 61 records); renters 15.1% a year (1.356% a month, 99 records). Monthly = 1 - (1 - annual)^(1/12). 0 of 96 types have their own rate (at least 30 records); 96 take their tenure's. Monthly rates range 0.446% to 1.356%.
Refill: out-movers' homes take households of the same types in proportion to the zone's departures (each type's rate times its households), so with no homes built or lost a zone keeps its type mix (stationary by construction).

### New homes

A new home's household type is drawn from PUMS 2024 households that moved in within 12 months into homes built from 2010 (the latest built-year code at or before 2024 - 10). Affordable homes take the same households at incomes at or below their tier's limit (50%, 80% or 120% of SF AMI 2024 for the household's size, MOHCD).

| Mix | Records | Households | Renters | Spaces per new home |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Market | 5 | 137 | 71.5% | 1.972 |
| Very low income | 3 | 61 | 36.1% | 2.311 |
| Low income | 5 | 137 | 71.5% | 1.972 |
| Moderate income | 5 | 137 | 71.5% | 1.972 |

Affordable homes by tier: very low 44.5%, low 55.5%, moderate 0.0%. The dataset's affordable completions by tier sum to 0, so these are the PUMS new-home movers at or below the moderate limit, split by tier.

### Parking in new buildings

Spaces per new home = predicted cars per household of the new-home mix (the choice and the zone's constants at its density) x 1.4 spaces built per space used (tier 3: King County Metro, "Right Size Parking Final Report", August 2015 (VIA Architecture), reproduced as Appendix A14 of the City of San Diego TPA Multifamily Residential Parking Standards Study, Appendix A).
Market mix today: 1.972 spaces per new home citywide (start-households weighted); by block group median 1.927, 10th to 90th percentile 1.903 to 2.222.
Baseline: each lot's reference is the spaces per home the model predicts for it at the window's start (today's households, today's transit). Today's starts are post-2018, built to demand, so predicted demand (not the old minimums, nor the parking the Controller prototypes assume) is the reference; only change from today moves start odds.

Cost per space (hard cost, cited SF figures), in 2026 dollars, the finance prototypes' (Controller 2026), since the odds shift divides it by their cost per home: cost x I(2026) / I(y) x CPI(2026) / CPI(y), y the source's dollars year. I is the Controller's Blended Construction Cost Index (market.json, inflation-adjusted, held at 2023 after its last year): the real change in construction cost. CPI is BLS CPI-U San Francisco-Oakland-Hayward, all items, annual average (CUURS49BSA0, cpi.json): the price level. The 2026 annual average is not yet published, so 2025's stands in for CPI(2026).

| Type | Cited | Dollars year | Cost index ratio | CPI ratio | 2026 dollars | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| podium | $30,000 | 2016 | 1.1230 | 1.3366 | $45,031 | invented |
| belowGrade | $70,000 | 2016 | 1.1230 | 1.3366 | $105,073 | invented |
| surface | none | none | none | none | none | no SF source found |

surface: no cited SF cost per space, so projects built with that parking get no parking cost (zero shift).
Cross-check, not used: the Controller's 2026 parking hard cost of $245 to $360 per gross square foot times about 400 square feet per space gives $98,000 to $144,000 per below-grade space in 2026 dollars (docs/dev/cars-data.md), beside the cited figure's $105,073.
